rules.title: Tenant Protection Act statewide just cause eviction requirement
rules.requirement: After a tenant has lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months (or 24 months for one tenant if adult tenants were added), the owner may terminate the tenancy only for an enumerated at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the written notice. Curable lease violations require a notice and opportunity to cure first.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 12 months of tenancy (24 months if new adult tenants were added)
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property in California, including mobilehome park units, where tenants have continuously and lawfully occupied the unit for 12 months (or one tenant for 24 months if adult tenants were added). Does not apply where a qualifying local just cause ordinance applies.
rules.exemptions: Transient/tourist hotels; nonprofit hospitals, religious, extended care and licensed residential care facilities; school/college dormitories; units where the tenant shares a bathroom or kitchen with the resident owner; single-family owner-occupied residences renting no more than two units or bedrooms (including ADU/JADU); owner-occupied duplexes where neither unit is an ADU/JADU; housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); separately alienable units (e.g., single-family homes, condos) not owned by a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, if the required exemption notice was given; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; mobilehome homeowners.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Requires 12 months continuous lawful occupancy (24 months for one tenant if adult tenants added); separately alienable unit exemption depends on non-corporate ownership and written exemption notice; owner-occupancy and shared-facility exemptions; deed-restricted/subsidized affordable housing excluded; displaced where a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before Sept 1, 2019 or a more protective later ordinance applies.

rules.penalty: Termination notice void for noncompliance; owner attempting recovery in material violation liable for actual damages, discretionary attorney's fees and costs, up to three times actual damages for willful/oppressive/fraudulent/malicious conduct, and punitive damages; Attorney General, city attorney or county counsel may seek injunctive relief.
rules.quoted_span: (a) Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.conflict_note: Section text states it became operative April 1, 2024; latest amendment (Stats. 2025, Ch. 203, AB 1529) effective January 1, 2026. Original Tenant Protection Act just cause rules date from 2020 (not stated in this document). Section sunsets and is repealed January 1, 2030.

rules.title: Relocation assistance or final-month rent waiver for no-fault just cause terminations
rules.requirement: When terminating a covered tenancy for no-fault just cause, the owner must, regardless of tenant income, either pay relocation assistance equal to one month's rent within 15 calendar days of the notice or waive the final month's rent in writing, and must notify the tenant of this right in the termination notice. Failure to strictly comply voids the notice.
rules.key_value: One month's rent, paid within 15 calendar days of notice (or final month rent waiver)
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies requiring just cause under Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2(a) terminated for owner/relative move-in, withdrawal from rental market, government/court order compliance, or demolition/substantial remodel.
rules.exemptions: Same exemptions as § 1946.2 generally; tenant not entitled where a government agency or court finds the tenant at fault for the condition triggering an order to vacate.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to no-fault terminations of tenancies with 12+ months occupancy that are subject to § 1946.2; exemptions for non-corporate separately alienable units with notice, owner-occupied properties, and deed-restricted/subsidized affordable housing; displaced by qualifying local just cause ordinances.

rules.penalty: Owner's failure to strictly comply renders the notice of termination void.
rules.quoted_span: (3) (A) The amount of relocation assistance or rent waiver shall be equal to one month of the tenant’s rent that was in effect when the owner issued the notice to terminate the tenancy.
rules.conflict_note: Section operative April 1, 2024 per subdivision (m); amended by AB 1529 effective January 1, 2026; repealed January 1, 2030. Credited against relocation assistance required by other law.

rules.title: Required tenant notice of rent cap and just cause protections
rules.requirement: Owners of property subject to § 1946.2 must give tenants a statutory notice, in at least 12-point type, stating that California limits rent increases (§ 1947.12) and requires just cause for termination (§ 1946.2), in the lease, an addendum, or a signed written notice.
rules.key_value: Statutory notice in no less than 12-point type
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies in residential real property subject to § 1946.2; for tenancies commenced or renewed on or after July 1, 2020 (July 1, 2022 for mobilehomes) in the lease, addendum, or signed notice; for existing tenancies by written notice by August 1, 2020 (August 1, 2022 for mobilehomes) or addendum.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to properties subject to § 1946.2 (non-exempt ownership, not deed-restricted affordable housing, not covered by qualifying local just cause ordinance); notice subject to translation requirements of Civ. Code § 1632.

rules.penalty: Failure to comply with any provision of the section renders the written termination notice void.

rules.conflict_note: Section operative April 1, 2024 per subdivision (m); notice deadlines date to 2020/2022; amended effective January 1, 2026; repealed January 1, 2030.
